en.name: Corn tortillas
en.summary: Shop-bought corn tortillas keep 25–45 days from purchase in the cupboard and 60–90 days refrigerated. They are one of the few breads that genuinely do better in the fridge, because the masa is already cooked and there is little fat to go stale.
en.pantry: A sealed pack keeps 25–45 days from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard, or to the printed date if that falls sooner. Once opened, keep the stack in its bag with the air pressed out and the end folded over, because exposed tortillas dry at the edges and crack the moment you fold them. Warm ones straight through on a dry pan or a comal rather than in the microwave if you want them pliable again — corn tortillas go leathery when reheated wet.
en.fridge: The fridge nearly doubles the window: 60–90 days from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, still in their sealed bag. This is the opposite of the usual advice about bread, and the reason is that a corn tortilla is cooked masa rather than a leavened wheat loaf — there is no crumb structure to go stale in the way refrigeration stales bread, and cold holds off the mould that usually ends a pack. Press the air out of the bag, keep the stack flat, and let the tortillas come back to room temperature or reheat them before use.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for corn tortillas here, so this page will not supply one — but they do freeze and will be safe indefinitely at −18 °C (0 °F). If you freeze them, interleave the tortillas with baking paper so you can take out a few at a time, and heat them straight from frozen on a dry pan. The refrigerated span is long enough that most households will never need the freezer.
en.thawing: Heat them straight from frozen on a dry pan until soft and steaming, or thaw the pack in the fridge. Do not thaw a stack on the counter, where the outside sheets sweat and stick together.
spoilage: Blue-green or white mould spots, which is how a pack of tortillas usually ends.
A sour or fermented smell on opening the bag.
Tortillas gone stiff, dry and cracking at the edges — stale rather than unsafe.
A slimy or tacky feel to the surface.
tips: Keep the pack in the fridge if you get through them slowly.
Press the air out of the bag and fold the end over rather than leaving it open.
Reheat on a dry pan, not in a wet microwave, to bring them back.
Check the middle of the stack for mould, not just the top tortilla.

faq.q: How long do corn tortillas keep?
faq.a: 25–45 days from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard, or 60–90 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

faq.q: Should corn tortillas be kept in the fridge?
faq.a: Yes, if you use them slowly — unlike a wheat loaf, they keep much longer cold, because cooked masa does not stale the way bread crumb does.

faq.q: How do you soften dried-out tortillas?
faq.a: Heat them one at a time on a dry pan until they steam and go pliable. Reheating them wet makes them leathery.

zh.name: 玉米薄餅
zh.summary: 市售玉米薄餅從購買日起算，放櫥櫃 25～45 天，冷藏 60～90 天。它是少數真的「放冰箱更好」的餅類，因為玉米麵團本來就熟了，油脂也少，不太會走味。
zh.pantry: 未拆封放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃，從購買日起算 25～45 天，若標示日期更早則以標示為準。開封後把整疊留在袋子裡、壓出空氣並把袋口折起來，因為暴露在空氣中的餅皮邊緣會變乾，一折就裂。想讓它恢復柔軟，請用乾鍋或鐵板直接加熱，而不是微波——玉米薄餅用濕熱復熱會變得像皮革。
zh.fridge: 冷藏幾乎讓期限加倍：維持密封包裝放 4 °C 以下，從購買日起算 60～90 天。這和一般「麵包不要冰」的建議正好相反，原因在於玉米薄餅是熟的玉米麵團，不是發酵的小麥麵包——它沒有那種會因低溫而老化的麵包組織，而低溫正好擋住通常終結一包餅皮的黴。請把袋內空氣壓出、整疊平放，使用前回溫或復熱。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給玉米薄餅的冷凍期限，本頁也不會補一個——但它確實可以冷凍，在 −18 °C 下安全性是無限期的。要凍的話，餅皮之間夾烘焙紙，方便一次拿幾張，並直接從冷凍用乾鍋加熱。不過冷藏的期限已經夠長，多數家庭根本用不到冷凍庫。
zh.thawing: 直接從冷凍放乾鍋加熱到變軟冒蒸氣，或整包放冷藏解凍。不要把整疊放在檯面上退冰，外層會出汗黏在一起。
spoilage: 出現藍綠色或白色霉點——這是一包餅皮最常見的結局。
拆袋時聞到酸味或發酵味。
餅皮變硬、變乾、邊緣龜裂——那是走味而不是不安全。
tips: 把袋內空氣壓掉、袋口折起來，不要敞著。
用乾鍋復熱，不要微波，口感才回得來。
檢查黴要翻到整疊中間，不要只看最上面那張。

faq.a: 從購買日起算，陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃 25～45 天，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 60～90 天。
吃得慢的話建議放。和小麥麵包不同，它冷藏可以放久得多，因為熟玉米麵團不會像麵包組織那樣老化。

faq.q: 變乾的玉米薄餅怎麼救？
faq.a: 一張一張放乾鍋加熱到冒蒸氣、變柔軟。用濕熱的方式復熱會讓它變得像皮革。
